mainTopic: Who the משנה of ערב פסח follows, and the argument over stopping a meal when שבת or יום טוב begins
overview: Our משנה says that on ערב פסח, from close to מנחה time, a person may not eat until nightfall. A ברייתא was brought against רב פפא's explanation of the משנה. The גמרא first suggests the ברייתא is a faulty text, but מרימר testifies that it was accepted as reliable. So רב פפא is rejected, and the גמרא goes back to רב הונא: the משנה follows רבי יוסי. Then רב הונא is challenged from רבי יוחנן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה on ערב פסח, which seems to show that רבי יוסי argues there too. The גמרא answers that their argument is only about stopping a meal already in progress (הפסקה), not about starting one. A ברייתא proves this argument exists and tells the story in עכו, where the הלכה was fixed like רבי יוסי. Finally, שמואל rules like neither side: you spread a cloth and make קידוש. The גמרא begins challenging this from another statement of שמואל, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא is a faulty text
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to protect רב פפא by suggesting that the ברייתא quoted against him was copied wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that ברייתא is corrupted (an unreliable version).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to brush off the ברייתא that was just used to attack רב פפא. It says the text of that ברייתא might simply be mistaken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treated ערב פסח exactly like ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב, which contradicts רב פפא's distinction between them. Instead of answering the logic, this step questions whether the source itself is reliable. If the ברייתא is a bad text, it cannot be used to challenge anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: a corrupted, unreliable text of a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is a defense of רב פפא against a ברייתא quoted on the previous amud, on the previous page.

phrases.english: Perhaps it (the baraita) is corrupted.
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא quoted just before, which equated ערב פסח with ערב שבת and ערב יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב פפא against the ברייתא challenge earlier.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא as valid evidence against רב פפא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's text may be corrupted.

steps.title: Testimony that the ברייתא is reliable
steps.stepSummary: מרימר (or רב יימר) testifies that this ברייתא was recited before רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי, and רב פנחס accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר, and some say רב יימר, said to him: I happened to come to the public lecture of רב פנחס, son of רב אמי. The תנא (the reciter of ברייתות) stood up and recited this ברייתא before him, and he accepted it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone answers the claim that the ברייתא is faulty. He says he personally heard it recited before a great teacher, who accepted it as correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion in step 1 depended on the ברייתא being an unreliable text. This eyewitness report shows that an authority accepted the ברייתא as accurate. That cancels the escape route from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: a public lecture (often on a יום טוב)
here: the official reciter who memorized ברייתות
and he accepted it from him (approved it as correct)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָרִימָר, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יֵימַר:
phrases.english: Mareimar said to him, and some say Rav Yeimar:
I happened to come to the lecture
of Rav Pinchas, son of Rav Ami,
and the tanna stood up and recited it before him,
and he accepted it from him.
phrases.notes: Since רב פנחס accepted it, the ברייתא is treated as a reliable text.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָרִימָר, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יֵימַר: אֲנָא אִיקְּלַעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim in step 1 that the ברייתא is corrupted.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא is an accurate, accepted text.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Eyewitness testimony that רב פנחס בריה דרב אמי accepted it when it was recited before him.

steps.title: רב פפא's approach falls, so the גמרא returns to רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא is reliable, the challenge against רב פפא stands. The clear explanation of the משנה is רב הונא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is difficult (the challenge against רב פפא stays). Rather, it is clear that the משנה follows the explanation of רב הונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that רב פפא's explanation cannot hold. It decides the משנה must be explained the way רב הונא said, as following רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא needed ערב פסח to be different from ערב שבת, but the reliable ברייתא makes them the same. So the משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה in the way רב פפא suggested. That leaves רב הונא's reading: רבי יוסי allows eating on ערב שבת but agrees it is forbidden on ערב פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: it is difficult (the challenge remains unanswered)
it is clear / the clear conclusion is

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is reliable, so רב פפא is rejected. The משנה follows רבי יוסי, as רב הונא explained.

phrases.english: If so, it is difficult!
Rather, it is clear that it is like Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי קַשְׁיָא! אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא כִּדְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of step 2: the challenge to רב פפא stands, so the גמרא adopts רב הונא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's explanation is rejected. The משנה is understood like רב הונא, as following רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Does רב הונא's explanation really work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא with רבי יוחנן's ruling: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה on ערב פסח and רבי יוסי on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב הונא, does it work out well? Didn't רבי ירמיה say in the name of רבי יוחנן (and some say רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא): The הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding ערב פסח, and the הלכה follows רבי יוסי regarding ערב שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns around and questions רב הונא too. It brings a ruling that seems to treat רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי as disagreeing even about ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's whole explanation rests on רבי יוסי agreeing that eating is forbidden on ערב פסח. רבי יוחנן gave separate rulings: like רבי יהודה for ערב פסח and like רבי יוסי for ערב שבת. Those separate rulings hint that the two תנאים argue in both cases. The next step spells out this hint.

keyTerms.meaning: does it work out well? (an opening for a challenge)
but didn't (so-and-so) say? (brings a source that contradicts)

phrases.english: And according to Rav Huna, does it work out well?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yirmeya say that Rabbi Yochanan said,
and some say Rabbi Abbahu said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda regarding the eve of Passover,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei regarding the eve of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב הוּנָא מִי נִיחָא? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of רב הונא that was just adopted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that רבי יוסי agrees eating is forbidden on ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן gave separate rulings for ערב פסח and ערב שבת, which suggests that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree in both cases.

steps.title: Inference: רבי יוסי disagrees even about ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the first half of the ruling and reasons that it was only needed if רבי יוסי argues on ערב פסח too. That undercuts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding ערב פסח.' This shows by implication that רבי יוסי disagrees in both cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ruling again in order to draw an inference from it. If the הלכה needed to be decided for ערב פסח, there must be a disagreement there, so רבי יוסי permits eating even on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה ruling is only needed where there is a dispute. Ruling like רבי יהודה on ערב פסח therefore means רבי יוסי argued there and allowed eating. That directly contradicts רב הונא, who said רבי יוסי agrees ערב פסח is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: The repeated line is not a new ruling. The גמרא repeats רבי יוחנן's words on purpose to draw the inference from them.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge holds, neither רב פפא nor רב הונא can explain whom the משנה follows. That pushes the סוגיא to find a new explanation.

phrases.english: 'The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda regarding the eve of Passover':
phrases.notes: This is the ruling from step 4, quoted again so the גמרא can draw a conclusion from it.

phrases.english: This implies that Rabbi Yosei disagrees in both cases!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּעֶרֶב הַפֶּסַח, מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיג רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the inference from the ruling quoted in step 4, which completes the challenge to רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that the משנה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A הלכה ruling for ערב פסח implies a dispute there, so רבי יוסי permits eating on ערב פסח and cannot be the author of the משנה.

steps.title: The argument is about stopping a meal, not starting one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge to רב הונא. The word 'הלכה' in רבי יוחנן's ruling shows there is an argument, but the argument is about interrupting a meal already in progress, not about starting to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. When רבי יוחנן says 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה', this shows that they argue about interrupting a meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. It says רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי do argue, but only about whether you must stop a meal you already started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 assumed that if they argue on ערב פסח, the argument must be about starting to eat. That would contradict רב הונא, who says everyone agrees not to start. The answer moves the argument to a different question: once you are already eating and the holy day begins, must you stop (הפסקה)? רב הונא's point about not starting stays intact.

keyTerms.meaning: Interrupting or stopping a meal that has already begun

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי allows you to start eating late on ערב פסח. According to this answer, he agrees you may not start. He only says that if you already started, you do not have to stop.

phrases.english: No: [when he said] 'the הלכה [follows רבי יהודה]',
phrases.notes: The גמרא rejects the reasoning of step 5 and rereads רבי יוחנן's word 'הלכה'.

phrases.english: this implies that they argue about interrupting.
phrases.notes: The argument is about stopping a meal in progress, not about starting one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the קשיא of step 5 and saves רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the subject of the dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's 'הלכה' implies that רבי יוסי allows you to start eating on ערב פסח, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'הלכה' refers to a separate argument about interrupting a meal already in progress. Both sides agree you may not start eating.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows they argue about interrupting a meal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי יהודה requires stopping a meal when שבת begins, while רבי יוסי says you do not have to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'You must stop for שבת,' says רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: 'You do not have to stop.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that an argument about stopping a meal really exists between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 claimed they argue about הפסקה. This ברייתא shows the argument in black and white. In רבי יהודה's view, you must stop when שבת begins (to make קידוש); רבי יוסי says you may finish your meal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a real source for the argument about הפסקה, so the answer in step 6 is not just a guess.

phrases.english: As it was taught: we interrupt [a meal] for Shabbat,
phrases.notes: Once שבת begins, you stop the meal to make קידוש.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: we do not interrupt.
phrases.notes: You may finish the meal you already started.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It proves the claim of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about interrupting a meal (הפסקה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'מפסיקין לשבתות, דברי רבי יהודה; רבי יוסי אומר אין מפסיקין'

steps.title: The story in Akko: should we stop the meal?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells a story. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי were eating together in עכו when שבת began. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asked רבי יוסי whether they should stop, out of respect for רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי were reclining at a meal in עכו, and the day became holy (שבת began). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to רבי יוסי: 'Great one, do you want us to stop and take into account the words of our friend יהודה?'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a real-life story. It sets up a question that רבי יוסי will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument from step 7 happens in real time: the three sages are in the middle of a meal when שבת arrives. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל suggests stopping to be careful about רבי יהודה's opinion, even though רבי יוסי holds you do not have to stop.

keyTerms.meaning: The day became holy for them (שבת began)
A title of honor for a distinguished scholar
Let us be concerned for, take into account

phrases.english: And there was an incident with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
[and Rabbi Yehuda] and Rabbi Yosei
who were reclining at a meal in Akko
and the day became sanctified upon them,
phrases.notes: שבת began while they were still eating.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said to Rabbi Yosei:
Great one, is it your wish that we stop
phrases.notes: בְּרַבִּי is a title of respect.

phrases.english: and take into account the words of our colleague Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the same ברייתא and shows the argument from step 7 happening in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When שבת began during their meal, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל proposed stopping, to be careful about רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's sharp reply
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל usually prefers רבי יוסי's opinions over רבי יהודה's. So how can he now favor רבי יהודה right in front of him? He quotes a verse from אסתר to make his point.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Every single day you prefer my words over רבי יהודה's, and now you prefer רבי יהודה's words in front of me? "Will he even conquer the queen with me in the house?"'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers the question from step 8. He refuses to stop the meal and objects to being overruled in his own presence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי points out that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל normally rules like him. Switching to רבי יהודה's view while sitting next to רבי יוסי feels like an insult to his honor. The verse from אסתר (what אחשורוש said about המן) makes the image sharp: it is like someone attacking the queen while the king himself is in the house. The next step gives רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's decision.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of me, in my presence

phrases.english: He said to him: Every single day

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה מְחַבֵּב דְּבָרַיי לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: you prefer my words over Rabbi Yehuda's,
and now you prefer
the words of Rabbi Yehuda in my presence?
"Will he even conquer the queen
phrases.notes: אסתר 7:8. אחשורוש's words when he found המן near אסתר.

phrases.english: with me in the house?"
phrases.notes: Meaning: you are overruling me right in front of me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם אַתָּה מְחַבֵּב דְּבָרַיי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's question from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the group should stop the meal out of concern for רבי יהודה's opinion
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. רבי יוסי objects to rejecting his view in his own presence, since his opinion is usually the one followed.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל decides not to stop the meal
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל accepts רבי יוסי's point. He decides they will not stop eating, so that students do not mistakenly learn that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, we will not stop eating. Otherwise the students may see us stop and fix the הלכה that way for all future generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers רבי יוסי's complaint from Step 9 and agrees not to interrupt the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He had wanted to stop only to show respect for רבי יהודה's view. But he realizes that what great rabbis do in public becomes a ruling. Students would copy them and treat it as the הלכה forever. So even a small act of being extra careful could falsely set the הלכה like רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will not interrupt / stop (the meal)
And they will fix the הלכה for generations

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle. When a leading rabbi acts in public, people treat it as a ruling. So he must be careful not to act in a way that misleads people about the real הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל speaking to רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: we will not interrupt,
phrases.notes: We will keep eating even though שבת has started.

phrases.english: lest the students see
phrases.notes: They would see us stop the meal.

phrases.english: and fix the halacha for generations.
phrases.notes: They would set the הלכה like רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם כֵּן לֹא נַפְסִיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוסי's protest in Step 9 by accepting it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We will not stop the meal, because stopping in front of students would set the הלכה like רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The הלכה was fixed like רבי יוסי on the spot
steps.stepSummary: The sages report that the rabbis did not leave that place until they had set the הלכה like רבי יוסי: you do not have to stop a meal when שבת begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: They did not move from there until they fixed the הלכה according to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends its story with the result: the הלכה was settled like רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story began as a question of respect for רבי יהודה. It ended with an official ruling for רבי יוסי. That ruling is that a meal begun before שבת does not have to be interrupted.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not move from there

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about stopping a meal once שבת or יום טוב begins (הפסקה), not about starting one. This lets רבי יוחנן's ruling fit with רב הונא's explanation. According to the ברייתא, the הלכה on הפסקה follows רבי יוסי: you do not stop a meal in progress.

phrases.english: They said: they did not move from there
phrases.notes: "They said" is the later sages reporting what happened.

phrases.english: until they established the halacha like Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: No need to stop the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: לֹא זָזוּ מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁקָּבְעוּ הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final outcome of the story that Step 10 continued.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא concludes that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי: a meal in progress need not be stopped for שבת.

steps.title: שמואל's middle ruling: cover the table and make קידוש
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules like neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי. Instead, you spread a cloth over the table, make קידוש, and then may continue eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה and not like רבי יוסי. Rather, you spread a cloth over the table and say קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא, שמואל, gives a new ruling that takes a middle path between the two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says you must truly stop the meal (the table is removed). רבי יוסי says you do not stop at all. שמואל says to cover the food with a cloth and make קידוש. That is a small pause to honor שבת, and then the meal goes on. So it is not a full stop, but it is also not ignoring שבת.

keyTerms.term: אֵין הֲלָכָה לֹא כְּ... וְלֹא כְּ...
keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is neither like this one nor like that one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל is siding with רבי יוסי just because the meal continues. He requires a real action, covering the table and making קידוש, which רבי יוסי did not require.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Yehuda
phrases.notes: Not a full stop of the meal.

phrases.english: and not like Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: Not ignoring שבת entirely.

phrases.english: rather, he spreads a cloth and makes kiddush.
phrases.notes: After that, he may continue eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין הֲלָכָה לֹא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְלֹא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא ruled like רבי יוסי, שמואל gives a different, in-between ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When שבת begins during a meal, you cover the table with a cloth, make קידוש, and continue eating.

steps.title: Challenge from another statement of שמואל about interrupting for קידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל really said this. It begins quoting רב תחליפא בר אבדימי in שמואל's name: "Just as one interrupts for קידוש..." The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But רב תחליפא בר אבדימי said in the name of שמואל: Just as we interrupt (the meal) for קידוש...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against שמואל's ruling from Step 12, using a different quote of שמואל. This step sets up a contradiction that is completed on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new quote speaks of "interrupting" (מפסיקין) for קידוש, which sounds like a real stop of the meal. That seems to clash with שמואל's milder rule of just covering the table. Wait for the rest of the quote and the answer on the next amud before deciding how the two fit together.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
phrases.notes: Opens the challenge.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi say
phrases.notes: Another student of שמואל's teachings.

phrases.english: that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: This is the same שמואל as in Step 12.

phrases.english: Just as one interrupts for kiddush,
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of שמואל just stated in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that you only spread a cloth and make קידוש (Step 12).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another quote of שמואל uses the language of interrupting the meal for קידוש. That seems to clash with his ruling here, so the two statements look contradictory. The full challenge is completed on the next amud.
